title: Understanding MSE on Test Data
text: Mean Squared Error (MSE) on held-out test data measures how well the model generalizes to unseen data. It is affected by both bias and variance.

title: Effect of Removing a Feature
text: Removing a feature can potentially increase bias because the model has less information to work with. However, it can also decrease variance by simplifying the model.

title: Balancing Bias and Variance
text: The trade-off between bias and variance is crucial. Removing a feature might increase bias but decrease variance, affecting the MSE on test data.

title: Possible Effects on MSE
text: Consider how removing a feature affects both bias and variance. What are the possible effects on MSE on held-out test data?
